Every other item depends on it.

items.docs: BL UI reads your shadcn theme variables (and --radius, --font-sans). For the iOS look add the bl-theme item. The "dark" variant is redefined to also match the element that carries .dark, so a ThemeScope root can restyle itself.

items.name: bl-theme
items.title: BL theme
items.description: BL UI's iOS look as a shadcn theme: sets your CSS variables (light and dark) to the iOS palette, plus the Workbench, terminal, sheet and glass theme scopes the Composer and floating chats use.

theme.font-sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', sans-serif

items.name: adaptive-pane
items.title: AdaptivePane
items.description: One pane presented as a column, a drawer, a page pushed over a compact host, a cover or hidden, chosen by its host or by the size class (auto), resizable, with its children kept mounted, and a header with a title and a close or back button.

items.name: animated-height
items.title: AnimatedHeight
items.description: Trays that change size instead of cutting: AnimatedHeight springs its height to its content (pair it with Swap to replace the content in the direction of travel).

items.name: append-stream
items.title: Append-only streams
items.description: Named, append-only lists of JSON records in localStorage: each write is a new chunk key (gzip when the browser can), so nothing stored is ever rewritten; a full store asks an evict callback for room. LocalStreams is the store the session recorder and Freeform write to.

items.name: artifact-chat-container
items.title: ArtifactChatContainer
items.description: The chat shell: a chat column docked beside an artifact on a wide container, a FloatingSheet over it on a compact one that peeks, grows and folds into a FAB, with the transcript and composer kept across the switch.

items.name: avatar-group
items.title: AvatarGroup
items.description: Avatars overlapping in a row, with a +N count past the limit; with `menu`, the stack is one button whose menu lists everyone.

items.name: avatar
items.title: Avatar
items.description: An avatar on UI SDK's Avatar: initials on a name-derived gradient (or a tint), an image, or a glyph, with a presence dot and an optional hover card. AvatarGroup stacks them.

items.name: badge
items.title: Badge
items.description: A small iOS capsule for a status, count or tag, in default, secondary, tinted, outline, destructive, success and warning variants, at two sizes (a single digit is a circle).

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb
items.description: The path to the current page: every item pressable, siblings in a menu like VS Code's, and the middle collapsing into a … menu when the trail does not fit.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: The labelled action button: UI SDK's Button with default, secondary, outline, contrast, ghost, quiet, destructive, plain (the iOS bar text button) and link (inline, in running text) variants, seven sizes including the full-width iOS pill and three square icon sizes, a pending state while its onClick Promise runs, a press that sinks on a spring, and a text label that morphs into the next one.

items.name: calendar
items.title: Calendar
items.description: A month calendar that picks one date, several, or a range: UI SDK's Calendar with keyboard navigation, locale week starts, min/max and unavailable dates, drawn as iOS round day cells with a soft band joining a range. Dates are ISO strings.

items.name: call-stack-model
items.title: CallStack logic
items.description: CallStack's logic as plain functions: which rows a list of frames shows, and how a location reads.

items.name: call-stack
items.title: CallStack
items.description: Frames as a debugger lists them: the top frame marked, runs of framework and library frames folded, async boundaries as labelled separators, short locations with the full path a press away. Virtualized, on UI SDK's Tree.

items.name: canvas-math
items.title: Canvas math
items.description: The frame math behind Canvas, as plain functions on plain data: board and screen coordinates for a view, hit tests (a point in a rotated frame, rectangles that intersect, distance to a segment or a polyline), selection handles and their cursors, resize, rotate, and snapping a box to its neighbours with alignment guides.

items.name: canvas
items.title: Canvas
items.description: An infinite, pannable, zoomable surface on UI SDK's viewport: scroll to pan, pinch or ⌘-scroll to zoom, Space to drag the view, zoom and arrow keys with announcements, focus and find in page brought into view, a controller to fit and zoom from outside, a dotted or ruled background that follows the view, and pointer events handed to you in board coordinates. With selection outlines, resize and rotate handles, a marquee, alignment guides and a minimap that keep their thickness at any zoom, pointer layers (a PencilCanvas inside it is its drawing layer), and the frame math (hit tests, resize, rotate, snap) as plain functions.

items.name: card
items.title: Card
items.description: An inset-grouped panel with header, title, description, action, content and footer parts, in default, elevated and outline variants.

items.name: celebrate
items.title: Celebrate
items.description: A confetti burst and pulsing ring around its child for rare moments, fired each time a value changes.

items.name: checkbox
items.title: Checkbox
items.description: UI SDK's Checkbox and CheckboxGroup with a round iOS selection mark (or a square one), a drawn-on tick and an indeterminate state.

items.name: cloudflare-diagram
items.title: CloudflareDiagram
items.description: Cloudflare's services on a Diagram: each a node with what it can call and receive as ports, from a catalog generated from Cloudflare's docs, Wrangler's schema and the Workers types. A connection can only be one the catalog says there is, and it offers the real methods. What it's given is a system, which saves as JSON and reads from and writes to wrangler.jsonc, or is read from a workerd config.capnp: it says what's wrong with one, and with editable a search of the catalog adds a service and a service's machine opens in a StateDiagram. Read-only by default: a picture to select in and read. Its board is also a Diagram preset, cloudflareBoardProps(system). No Cloudflare artwork. ELK and XState are optional peers.

items.name: code-editor-gpu
items.title: CodeEditor GPU highlighting
items.description: A highlighter for CodeEditor's windowed renderer on gpu-lexer. It answers a frame late, and where there's no WebGPU the editor stays plain text.

items.name: code-editor-model
items.title: CodeEditor logic
items.description: CodeEditor's logic as plain functions: splitting lines, windowing long lines, its selection model, a lexer that can resume in the middle of a long line, and a document with commands and undo.

items.name: code-editor
items.title: CodeEditor
items.description: Code you can edit, and read-only code of any shape, with one API and two renderers: in the page for a snippet or inline code, and windowed for an editor or a source view, smooth on a megabyte line and on half a million lines, with gutters, a current line, markers, undo and input methods.

items.name: color-picker
items.title: ColorPicker
items.description: UI SDK's ColorPicker drawn as iOS: an area, channel sliders, preset swatches, typed and per-channel inputs in the kit's field box and an eye dropper that edit one CSS color; a trigger and popover the root opens; ColorInput, the one-line typed color field; and ColorSwatch, a chip on its own.

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: A filterable text field with a suggestion list: UI SDK's Combobox, composed from a field (the kit's field box, in three sizes), its input, disclosure and clear buttons and chips. Type to narrow the options (by label and keywords), arrow keys to move, Enter to choose, with options from data, an empty state, multiple choice and custom values.

items.name: command-menu
items.title: CommandMenu
items.description: A command palette on UI SDK's Command: fuzzy search with matches in bold, nested pages with Back, shortcuts, grid groups, ⌘1–9, a keyboard legend, inline or in a ⌘K dialog.

items.name: composer
items.title: Composer
items.description: A prompt box as parts: a card with the Docstream editor, attachment tiles (images open the ImageAnnotator), footer option pills on the kit's DropdownMenu, send / stop / add buttons on the kit's Button, bumps above and below, a queue for drafts sent while a reply streams, and compact and FAB collapse.

items.name: conversation
items.title: Conversation
items.description: An agent thread around one composer: an empty state (the kit's EmptyState) over a centred composer that flies down to its dock when the first message arrives, then a MessageScroller of user and assistant turns with attachments, streaming markdown, a work log and tool calls.

items.name: cron-editor
items.title: CronEditor
items.description: Edit a 5-field cron expression with its meaning in view: per-field labels and validation, an English description, presets and the next runs in any time zone, all local. Where WebGPU is available, a plain-English box (gpu-cron) proposes an expression to review.

items.name: cron
items.title: Cron
items.description: Cron expressions, locally and without React: validate a 5-field expression field by field, list its next runs in any IANA time zone (POSIX day-of-month / day-of-week semantics, DST gaps and repeats handled), and describe it in English. Runs in server components.

items.name: csv
items.title: CSV
items.description: CSV and TSV as rows of strings (RFC 4180): quoted fields, "" escapes and line breaks inside quotes, CRLF or LF, a BOM, and delimiter detection. parseCsv remembers how the text was written so stringifyCsv writes an edited table back the same way.

items.name: data-table-model
items.title: DataTable logic
items.description: DataTable's logic as plain functions: the stable, empty-last sort of rows by a column, and the types of a sort, a column's size and a time range.

items.name: data-table
items.title: DataTable
items.description: A virtualized table of rows on UI SDK's virtualizer, grid focus and resize: typed columns (fixed or flexible widths, a header and a cell, as TanStack's ColumnDef, a sort value), sort, column resize, single selection or none, density, a size class of its own (bindSizeClass) that hides columns and stacks the rows when it is narrow, a toolbar, a footer, a loading state and an EmptyState, and an optional current time for rows on a timeline. An APG grid with one tab stop and cell focus (or row focus). Stays smooth at 100,000 rows. RequestTable and the SQL console's results are presets of it.

items.name: date-input
items.title: DateInput
items.description: Segmented date and time inputs: UI SDK's Date Input and Time Input, each part of the value its own spin-button input, in the kit's filled field. Values are ISO strings; a Field wires the label, description and error.

items.name: date-picker
items.title: DatePicker
items.description: A date input with a calendar button that opens a Calendar in a popup, for one date or a range: UI SDK's Date Picker, composed from a field box (the kit's filled field, sized with `size` on `DatePickerInputGroup`), its input and trigger, and a content part that takes every Calendar part.

items.name: debug-toolbar
items.title: DebugToolbar
items.description: A paused debugger's stepping controls with Codicons, as a preset of Toolbar: pick the actions, or compose your own row.

items.name: diagram-frame
items.title: DiagramFrame
items.description: A board with a panel: flat parts on AdaptivePane, so the panel is a column beside the board when there's the room, a drawer over it that doesn't dim it at medium sizes, and a page pushed over it on a phone. A bar on the board opens it (and a Diagram's fit leaves room for it), a cover with a back bar goes over everything, and titled sections fill the panel, with the kit's Field and Input (onValueCommit) for its fields.

items.name: diagram-layout
items.title: Diagram layout
items.description: Places a Diagram's nodes and routes its edges with ELK, in a Web Worker, measuring their words first. ELK is 442 KB gzipped and licensed EPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0-or-later, so it's only loaded when a layout's first asked for, and this item is what installs it.

items.name: diagram-model
items.title: Diagram model
items.description: Diagram's data as plain functions on plain nodes, ports and edges: index a diagram, measure its bounds, move nodes and edge ends, check and add a connection, delete a selection (with what it leaves dangling), and the geometry of every connector (routes, curves, arrowheads, hit tests). Nothing renders; Diagram, Freeform's connectors and Interface Builder's segues run on it.

items.name: diagram
items.title: Diagram
items.description: Nodes, edges, labels and regions on a Canvas, as plain data, on one primitive (data, selection, history) with a controller and agent actions. Generic looks (a node's kind and border, an edge's line and tone), lines that keep their thickness at any zoom, labels and routes that keep clear of the nodes, and above 200 items only what's near the view is drawn. Read-only, it selects and reads; with editable: dragging, deleting and undo as one gesture, named ports, and connecting with validation; every change goes through onDataChange(data, details) and can be refused. One history: its own, or one handed to it (useDiagramHistory), driven by ⌘Z and DiagramToolbar's zoom, fit, undo and redo, with a fit that leaves room for the toolbar. One tab stop: every node and edge is reached by keyboard and says what it connects to; focus, selection and what's current are drawn three ways.

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: Modal dialogs on UI SDK: Dialog, a card with a header, a scrolling body and footer actions that becomes a draggable tray in a compact container (presentation="auto"), with views that morph its height and travel in the direction of the flow (view, DialogView, DialogBack); AlertDialog, the centered iOS alert that waits for an answer; and the surface recipes the kit's other modal surfaces share.

items.name: disclosure
items.title: Disclosure
items.description: Expandable sections on UI SDK: a Disclosure (Collapsible) with a trigger and an animated panel, and a DisclosureGroup (Accordion) of them.

items.name: dropdown-menu
items.title: DropdownMenu
items.description: UI SDK's Menu drawn as an iOS pull-down menu: rows with trailing icons, descriptions and platform shortcuts, group bands, checkbox and radio items, submenus, menus from data, two sizes, a context-menu trigger (right-click, long press, Shift+F10), and a sheet on small touch screens.

items.name: durable-streams
items.title: Durable Streams sync
items.description: The cloud end of append-only streams: a client for the Durable Streams HTTP protocol, and CloudSync, which mirrors this browser's LocalStreams to such a server with idempotent producer writes and reads other devices' streams back. Off until a server URL is saved; useCloud(cloud) is its status and settings in React.

items.name: empty-state
items.title: EmptyState
items.description: What a list, table, tree, popup, pane or page shows when it has nothing: an optional icon, a title, a description and an action, in three sizes, AA on every surface. renderEmptyState(value, defaults) is how every emptyState prop in the kit is read (a string is the title, null nothing), as a polite status.

items.name: ffmpeg
items.title: FFmpeg
items.description: FFmpeg and FFprobe in the browser (openclaw/ffmpeg-wasm, built for the web by tools/ffmpeg-wasm), run like a command line in a pool of module workers: files in (Blobs mounted, never copied), the files a run wrote out, with progress and cancelling. Probes media, grabs filmstrip frames and decodes waveform peaks, with a React provider and hooks that share the work per file. Installs ffmpeg-worker.js into public/ffmpeg/; serve the wasm build next to it, from a cross-origin isolated page.

items.name: field
items.title: Field
items.description: UI SDK's Field restyled: the wrapper that links a FieldLabel, a control (Input, Textarea, Select, Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroup), a FieldDescription and a FieldError, names the control and shows validation; plus FieldSet, FieldLegend and FieldGroup for iOS-style grouped sections.

items.name: file-icons
items.title: File icons
items.description: File and folder glyphs: a tinted type icon picked from the file name, a document badge with its extension, and an open or closed folder.

items.name: file-size
items.title: File size
items.description: A file size the way every part of the kit writes it: decimal units in the reader's locale ("280 B", "627 kB", "1.3 MB"), the steps of UI SDK's formatFileSize, empty when the size is unknown.

items.name: file-upload
items.title: FileUpload
items.description: Pick, drop or paste files on UI SDK's FileInput: a styled dropzone and Browse trigger, a file list with previews, progress, retry and remove (one Tab stop, Delete removes), rejected files listed with their reasons, folder drops, and a concurrency-limited upload queue with an XHR adapter that reports real progress. Put the dropzone in a Field for its invalid state and error.

items.name: filmstrip
items.title: Filmstrip
items.description: A row of video frames across a stretch of media time: tiles its width with frame-shaped cells, each showing the frame nearest its time, so it reads right at any width or zoom.

items.name: filter-input
items.title: FilterInput
items.description: A natural-language box for Filter: type a sentence and see the chips it would create — what was understood, what was dropped, what was assumed — then press Enter to apply. Runs gpu-query, a 29,597-parameter tagger, in the browser on the CPU; a feasibility-spike model, so the preview is the point.

items.name: filter-model
items.title: Filter model
items.description: The data model behind Filter, with no UI: fields, filters, operator tables per kind, matchFilters (all/any), describeFilter, date presets, and a URL-safe serialize/parse that round-trips.

items.name: filter-query
items.title: Filter query
items.description: useFilterQuery: a typed sentence as Filter[] through gpu-query — debounced, stale-guarded, SSR-safe, the ~40 KB model fetched on first use — with the field-schema and clause-to-filter mapping (fuzzy option matching, dates, numbers) and a report of what it could not use.

items.name: filter
items.title: Filter
items.description: Linear-style filtering on UI SDK: a Filter button (and F shortcut) opens a searchable Command of fields, then a searchable multi-select of values (an option search: the field keeps focus, the arrows move, Enter ticks); each filter is a chip with its own operator menu and value popover, removable with ×, Backspace or Delete. One Toolbar tab stop with arrow keys across the chips, announcements through UI SDK's announce(), change details with reason, source, event and cancel(), match all/any and Clear all.

items.name: floating-sheet
items.title: FloatingSheet
items.description: A floating card that grows into the full page along one drag, over a map or canvas: UI SDK's Drawer with snap points, modal only above its peek, folding into a FAB.

items.name: font-picker
items.title: FontPicker
items.description: Google Fonts families picked the way a design tool picks them: a searchable, category-filtered list of the most popular families (the kit's CommandMenu, virtualized), each drawn in its own face (only its name's glyphs are fetched, only while on screen), that previews the highlighted family on your text. FontPicker holds one family (a root, its trigger and its popup), FontStackPicker a font stack (a root, its field of chips and its popup) as chips you reorder by their handle (drag, or Space and the arrows) or remove, FontList is the list alone; useGoogleFont and fontStack load and set a family without a picker.

items.name: google-fonts
items.title: Google Fonts
items.description: The most popular Google Fonts families (GOOGLE_FONTS, with category, weights and italics), loading one from the Google Fonts CDN once and only the glyphs a sample needs, and fontStack(family) for a CSS font-family with the right fallback. useGoogleFont and useGoogleFontStatus load a family from a component.

items.name: gpu-cron
items.title: Natural language to cron
items.description: Plain English to a 5-field cron expression, by gpu-cron (an 89 KB WebGPU model, no CPU fallback): gpuCronAvailable asks first without downloading anything on a browser with no WebGPU, parseCronText proposes an expression, and useCronParse is the debounced React side CronEditor uses.

items.name: gpu-query
items.title: gpu-query
items.description: A vendored copy of safzanpirani/gpu-query's runtime (MIT): a 29,597-parameter neural tagger that turns a phrase into filter clauses against your schema, on the CPU or WebGPU. The ~40 KB weights load lazily. A feasibility spike; see lib/gpu-query/README.md for provenance and what changed.

items.name: gpu-time
items.title: Natural-language times
items.description: Dates, times and recurrences written in English, parsed by gpu-time (a ~50 KB model, CPU by default, loaded on first use): parseTime resolves occurrences, RRULEs and the recognised spans; formatOccurrence, describeRecurrence and timeTextSegments turn the result into text. useTimeParse is the debounced React side NaturalTimeInput uses.

items.name: hover-card
items.title: Hover Card
items.description: A card that previews what a trigger points at (a person, link, file or commit) while the pointer rests on it or keyboard focus stays on it, on UI SDK's Hover Card; the pointer can move into it, one card can serve many triggers, and touch never opens it.

items.name: icon
items.title: Icons
items.description: An SF Symbols-style icon set on a 24px grid: round-capped strokes in six weights, filled variants, and custom shapes, and a Chevron that turns to face a new direction.

items.name: index-bar
items.title: IndexBar
items.description: A jump rail for long scrollers: the UIKit A-Z index, custom stops with previews, or a Dock-style wave of dashes with an outline panel.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: iOS filled text input on UI SDK's Input: three sizes, a primary focus ring, red invalid and dimmed disabled states, onValueChange with a reason and cancel, onValueCommit for a field that changes something once you're done (Enter or blur commits, Escape reverts), and a controller; inside a Field it is wired to its label, description and error.

items.name: kbd
items.title: Kbd
items.description: A keycap for keyboard shortcuts, with a group wrapper for chords; `keys` shows a UI SDK shortcut string for the reader's platform (⌘K or Ctrl+K).

items.name: kept-children
items.title: useKeptChildren
items.description: Children that survive a change of presentation: rendered once through a portal into a detached element that the current home docks, so a draft, the caret, scroll and a streaming reply stay mounted while a region moves between a column, a drawer, a pushed page or a floating sheet. The kit's one way to keep children mounted (AdaptivePane, Sidebar, ArtifactChatContainer).

items.name: label
items.title: Label
items.description: UI SDK's Label, a native label that names any control (by htmlFor or by wrapping it), in default, iOS grouped-form and control-row variants.

items.name: list
items.title: List
items.description: Inset-grouped and plain lists on UI SDK: sections that are lists of rows (grow in, collapse out, reorder by a grip with createReorder), rows with swipe actions and full swipe (createSwipeActions), edit mode and a hover preview, and an A-Z IndexBar.

items.name: listbox
items.title: Listbox
items.description: UI SDK's Listbox with single or multiple selection: an iOS inset-grouped list with trailing checks, or the compact popup list Select and Combobox draw. Groups, separators and options from data.

items.name: log-list-model
items.title: LogList logic
items.description: LogList's logic as plain functions: levels and their counts, a row's text and time, and what LogList and RequestTable share for their rows: how a list changed, rows by id, and how a followed marker scrolls.

items.name: log-list
items.title: LogList
items.description: A virtualized log on UI SDK's virtualizer, grid focus and stick-to-bottom: levels, times, sources and rich messages in rows of any height, a you-are-here marker that dims what comes after it and moves without re-rendering, following with a way back, keyboard navigation and copying. Stays smooth at 100,000 rows.

items.name: markdown-editor
items.title: MarkdownEditor
items.description: A themed WYSIWYG Markdown editor over docstream-editor: slash menu, Markdown paste, inline or chip images, and the built-in formatting toolbar or one of your own (a Toolbar of MarkdownEditorToolbarButtons).

items.name: markdown-view
items.title: MarkdownView
items.description: Read-only GitBook-flavored Markdown rendered by Docstream: headings, lists, tables, hints, tabs, highlighted code, live demos and reference chips, whole or streamed.

items.name: message-scroller
items.title: MessageScroller
items.description: A chat transcript that anchors each new turn near the top, follows the live edge only while the reader is there, and brings them back with a jump pill that says when a reply is streaming.

items.name: morph
items.title: Morph
items.description: Shared-element transitions: one element springs between two layouts (mini player → full player), drag-to-dismiss friendly, reduced-motion aware.

items.name: motion
items.title: Motion
items.description: Springs and the motion vocabulary: TextMorph, NumberMorph, Swap, Chevron, AnimatedHeight, Celebrate.

items.name: natural-time-input
items.title: NaturalTimeInput
items.description: A text field that reads dates, times and recurrences written in English ("every weekday at 9am") with gpu-time, and previews what it understood: the recognised words, the resolved occurrences in a time zone, a Repeats chip and the parser's notes. Put it in a Field for its label, description and error. Works on the CPU or the GPU; the package loads on first use.

items.name: navigation-stack
items.title: NavigationStack
items.description: iOS's navigation controller as composable parts, on a UI SDK primitive: pages pushed and popped by key (declared as children or drawn by renderPage), with large titles that collapse into the bar, a back button that names the page behind and a title that flies into it, a bar that rides away on scroll, pull to refresh, and Escape, platform back and edge-swipe pops that go to the innermost stack first; the stack of a SplitView column that pushes.

items.name: now-playing-bars
items.title: NowPlayingBars
items.description: The animated equaliser beside the track that's playing — still when paused and under reduced motion — plus the Slider tones for media controls.

items.name: number-morph
items.title: NumberMorph
items.description: A formatted number whose digits roll and whose separators slide as the value changes, using Intl.NumberFormat for currency, percent and compact notation.

items.name: object-tree-model
items.title: ObjectTree logic
items.description: ObjectTree's logic as plain functions: nodes, ranges for large collections, what's loaded and open, the rows they make, and nodes from any live value.

items.name: object-tree-value
items.title: Value previews
items.description: Values described as data, and the one-line previews a debugger shows for them (DevTools-style tokens, clipped strings, lengths of large collections): what ObjectValue draws and ObjectTree's rows use. No React and nothing about trees, so a console row can use it alone.

items.name: object-tree
items.title: ObjectTree
items.description: Values as a debugger shows them: scopes in collapsible sections, lazy children with loading and failed states, DevTools-style previews, getters, ranges for large collections, keyboard navigation and copying. Takes plain data, and any JSON-like value.

items.name: object-value
items.title: ObjectValue
items.description: A value's one-line preview, tinted by type as DevTools does, for strings, numbers, objects, arrays, maps, sets, dates, regexps, errors, symbols and more. Long strings truncate, with Show more and Copy.

items.name: open-code
items.title: OpenCode
items.description: OpenCode's real terminal UI (OpenTUI WebAssembly) on a browser workspace container, with the apps its servers open shown as live previews in a sandboxed frame beside it; Start / Stop, encrypted keychain stores and Agent Browser-compatible MCP tools.

items.name: passkey-vault
items.title: Passkey vault
items.description: Encrypted in-browser storage unlocked by a WebAuthn passkey (PRF): a random data key wrapped per passkey and by a recovery key, AES-GCM records in IndexedDB, hooks, and the enroll, unlock and gate screens.

items.name: pencilkit
items.title: PencilKit
items.description: Pressure-aware freehand drawing (perfect-freehand): PencilCanvas on its own or as a Canvas's drawing layer, the PencilKit tool palette (tools, inks, widths, undo/redo) on the kit Toolbar that folds to fit a phone, snapshot undo history, and the ImageAnnotator lightbox that marks up an image and saves it flattened.

items.name: persistent-state
items.title: Persistent state
items.description: State that survives a reload: usePersistentState is useState backed by localStorage as JSON (a missing, unparseable or invalid value falls back to the initial one; storage that throws is ignored), and loadJSON / saveJSON are the reads and writes underneath.

items.name: pglite
items.title: PGlite
items.description: Postgres in the browser, as React hooks: PGliteProvider opens a PGlite database lazily (StrictMode-safe, memory, IndexedDB or OPFS, optional worker), with useQuery, useLiveQuery, useExec, useTransaction, migrations, multi-tab locking, SQL / data-directory export and import, and schema introspection. Needs the @electric-sql/pglite package (installed with the item).

items.name: playback
items.title: Playback clock
items.description: The time a preview, a timeline and transport controls share: play, pause, seek, rate and loop on animation frames, as a small external store whose subscribers follow every tick without re-rendering.

items.name: popover
items.title: Popover
items.description: A floating panel anchored to its trigger, on UI SDK's Popover: a padded panel or a bare surface that flips to stay on screen, with a title, a description and an optional arrow; it can open on hover, serve many triggers through a controller, and become a bottom sheet in a compact container.

items.name: progress-ring
items.title: ProgressRing
items.description: Circular progress on UI SDK's Progress: a determinate ring that springs to each value with a rolling percentage, and a CountdownRing that drains second by second and turns red when it is urgent.

items.name: progress-stepper
items.title: ProgressStepper
items.description: A row of milestones for a multi-step process, as filling bars or a joined line, with complete, current and upcoming states; from a steps array or composed from ProgressStepperItem parts with your own icon, label and description.

items.name: progress
items.title: Progress
items.description: iOS progress bar on UI SDK's Progress: a label, a springing fill with a rolling percentage, three sizes, tones and an indeterminate sliding bar.

items.name: qr-code
items.title: QRCode
items.description: A real, scannable QR code rendered as SVG paths in currentColor, with rounded or square modules and four error-correction levels; text too long to encode renders an empty, invalid code and calls onError.

items.name: qr
items.title: QR encoder
items.description: A QR Code encoder (byte mode, the four error-correction levels), ported from Project Nayuki's library: encodeQR(text) returns the module matrix QRCode draws, or null when the text is too long for a code.

items.name: radio-group
items.title: RadioGroup
items.description: UI SDK's RadioGroup and Radio: round radios with one tab stop and arrow-key selection, vertical or horizontal.

items.name: replay-preview
items.title: ReplayPreview
items.description: An rrweb session replay in a browser frame: a URL bar that follows the recording, play/pause, a scrubber with click, error, failed-request and navigation markers, speed, fullscreen, Console and Network buttons that open a DevTools panel cut at the playhead (requests, failures, errors), a drawn cursor with click ripples, and a skeleton poster while the player loads.

items.name: request-table-model
items.title: RequestTable logic
items.description: RequestTable's logic as plain functions: names, sizes, status text, tones, each built-in column's sort value and the time range rows cover.

items.name: request-table
items.title: RequestTable
items.description: A network pane, as a preset of DataTable: the request columns (name, method, status, type, size, time), a waterfall on a shared time range, a current-time line that moves without re-rendering a row, links to the other end of a call, and two-line rows with a small waterfall when the table is narrow. Sorting, resizing, selection, the keyboard and virtual rows are DataTable's. Stays smooth at 10,000 rows.

items.name: scroll-area
items.title: ScrollArea
items.description: A scroll container on UI SDK's ScrollArea with the kit's thin scrollbars: native scrolling, overflow and edge state, optional overlay scrollbars and stick-to-end.

items.name: search-input
items.title: SearchInput
items.description: iOS search field on UI SDK's Input, InputGroup and InputClear: magnifier, clear button, Esc to clear (only when there is a query), Enter to submit, three sizes, controlled or uncontrolled.

items.name: segmented
items.title: Segmented
items.description: The iOS segmented control on UI SDK's SegmentedControl: one value, one tab stop, arrows move and select, three sizes on Button's heights, and the selected card slides and resizes between segments. Its track, segment and card recipes also draw Tabs `segmented` and ToggleGroup `filled`.

items.name: select
items.title: Select
items.description: A pop-up button that opens a list of options: UI SDK's Select with a filled (the kit's field box, in three sizes) or plain trigger, groups, options with icons and descriptions or from data, dense rows, typeahead on the closed button, Field integration and a sheet on small touch screens.

items.name: separator
items.title: Separator
items.description: A hairline rule on UI SDK's Separator, horizontal or vertical, decorative or announced, with an inset option that indents like an iOS list separator.

items.name: session-recorder
items.title: Session recorder
items.description: Records the page with rrweb, one session per page load, into append-only streams in localStorage (an index stream and one stream of events per session), optionally mirrored to a Durable Streams server. useSessionRecording, useSessions and useSessionCloud are the React side; the functions read, delete and measure what is stored.

items.name: sheet
items.title: Sheet
items.description: A modal panel pinned to an edge, on UI SDK's Drawer: the iOS card sheet with a grabber at the bottom, side panels on the left and right, or a drop-down from the top; it follows a drag, rests on snap points and springs away, and a short sheet springs to its content (SheetView), through the views of a flow. `contained` keeps it inside its parent box, and the panel variant is the edge drawer of a sidebar or menu.

items.name: sidebar
items.title: Sidebar
items.description: An app's navigation column, docked, as a collapsible icon rail or as a floating card, that becomes a drawer while its provider is compact: workspace, search with a shortcut, labelled sections and rows with icons, counts and a current page.

items.name: skeleton
items.title: Skeleton
items.description: Loading placeholders with a soft left-to-right sweep instead of a pulse: text lines, circles, rects and rounded blocks, and a SkeletonText paragraph with a shorter last line.

items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.description: UI SDK Slider with the iOS look: a 4px track, tint fill and 26px thumb, one or two thumbs, horizontal or vertical, plus a translucent overlay look for media controls that follows the color scheme (or a fixed appearance), a small scrubber size and --bl-slider-* color variables.

items.name: spinner
items.title: Spinner
items.description: Loading indicators: the iOS activity indicator (eight fading spokes in discrete steps, the default) and twenty-two CSS loaders with three patterns each: seven ported from Dani Asyrofi's Loading (Orbit, Bars, Matrix, Merge, Encode, Scan, Lift) and fifteen of BL UI's own (Steps, Cradle, Hourglass, Balance, Fanout, Battery, Bloom, Sonar, Gyro, Coalesce, Crystal, Loop, Relay, Robot, Kettle). They draw in currentColor, scale to any size, take a speed, pause themselves off screen, and hold still under reduced motion.

items.name: split-view
items.title: SplitView
items.description: UISplitViewController as composable parts, on a UI SDK primitive: sidebar, supplementary and detail columns that tile, float the sidebar or collapse into a push/pop stack by the size class of their own box, with keyboard-resizable dividers, back, Escape and edge-swipe navigation, columns that never remount, and NavigationStack as the stack of a column that pushes.

items.name: spreadsheet-model
items.title: Spreadsheet model
items.description: The data side of Spreadsheet, with no UI: column types, reading cells as numbers and dates, exact order-preserving 64-bit sort keys, sortRows (a WebGPU bitonic sort for number and date columns, natural text order on the CPU), selection statistics and column histograms tallied on the GPU, each with a CPU fallback that gives the same answer.

items.name: spreadsheet
items.title: Spreadsheet
items.description: A virtualized grid of string cells for CSV-sized and million-row data, as one primitive on UI SDK's grid focus, cell range, inline edit, undo stack, resize and virtualizer: an ARIA grid with one tab stop, keyboard navigation, range selection with announcements, in-place editing, tab-separated copy / cut / paste, undo, resizable columns and a controller. Sorting a number or date column is an exact 64-bit bitonic sort in a WebGPU compute shader, and number columns show histograms tallied on the GPU; both fall back to the CPU with the same answers. A controlled sort (sort / onSortChange), an EmptyState, and a status bar that shows the selection's sum and average and which engine sorted.

items.name: sql-console
items.title: SqlConsole
items.description: A SQL workbench for a PGlite database, made of parts: a header with the versions and a Database menu (SQL / data-directory export and import), a sidebar with the schema (a Tree over schemaTreeItems) and the history, the SqlConsoleEditor (a highlighted textarea on UI SDK's Textarea: ⌘/Ctrl+Enter runs, ↑/↓ history, an error squiggle and invalid state, a footer part; also usable on its own) and a DataTable per statement with typed headers, type-aware cells, labelled stacked rows and CSV / JSON copy, or the error with its line, caret, SQLSTATE and hint. Its text is controlled or uncontrolled (value / defaultValue / onValueChange).

items.name: state-diagram-model
items.title: StateDiagram logic
items.description: StateDiagram's logic as plain functions: an XState machine's source read without running it (parseXState), a machine as Diagram nodes and edges (machineToDraft), a simulation with stand-ins for everything it names, and edits to a machine's config that XState checks. Babel reads the source; XState is handed in, never imported.

items.name: state-diagram
items.title: StateDiagram
items.description: An XState machine on a Diagram, drawn from machine.root: compound and parallel states, initial markers, final states, and all of always, after, invoke and guards labelled. A machine or its JSON config, which can be run with stand-ins for all it names, and edited, writing to the config. XState and ELK are optional peers.

items.name: stl-viewer
items.title: StlViewer
items.description: A 3D preview of an .stl model, binary or ASCII: WebGL, drag to orbit, pinch or ⌘-scroll to zoom, double-click to reset, and the triangle count and size under it. The model takes the theme's primary color. A re-export of the viewer at @brett_lamy/ui/docstream/stl.

items.name: strudel-player
items.title: StrudelPlayer
items.description: An audio player for a Strudel live-coded pattern, inline code or a .strudel file: play/stop, a scrolling piano roll, the code, and an equipment rack. Strudel runs in the page, loaded on the first play; one pattern plays at a time. A re-export of the player at @brett_lamy/ui/docstream/strudel and the functions that drive its runtime.

items.name: surface
items.title: Surface parts
items.description: The header, title, description, body, footer, close button and sheet grabber recipes every modal surface and card shares (Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, AdaptivePane, Card, Popover, HoverCard, Toast). A hook-free module, so Server Components can use it; Dialog re-exports it.

items.name: swap
items.title: Swap
items.description: Content that changes in place, keyed by value: the slide effect moves the leaving view out and the next one in, in the direction of travel, and the pop effect shrinks and blurs one glyph out as the next grows in. The leaving view is hidden from assistive technology and focus while it exits.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: The iOS switch on UI SDK's Switch: a 51 by 31 track (38 by 22 at size sm), a SwitchThumb that springs across and stretches while pressed, labelled by its ListRow inside one.

items.name: syntax-lexer
items.title: Syntax lexer
items.description: The kit's synchronous, dependency-free syntax lexer: gpu-lexer's token classes for ts / js, json, css, html, bash, python, sql, markdown and yaml, and a C-family default for the rest. CodeEditor's fallback and docstream's code fences both color with it.

items.name: syntax
items.title: Syntax highlighting
items.description: Syntax lexing for code: gpu-lexer (a small WebGPU model that labels spans in any language) behind one shared device, queue and cache, with the kit's synchronous lexer (lib/syntax-lexer) as the fallback when WebGPU is missing or software-only. lexSyntax labels a source; tokenizeLines splits the spans into CodeEditor's per-line tokens; languageFromPath picks a language from a file name.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: Tabs on UI SDK, one component for every look: an iOS segmented control, a tinted underline, the iOS tab bar, a rail, a workspace rail or plain, on any side, with a sliding selection indicator, directional panels that keep their scroll, actions, a header and footer, and a bar that hides on scroll.

items.name: tailscale-connect
items.title: Tailscale WebAssembly client
items.description: The real tailnet client for createTailscale: adapts @agent-wasm/tailscale-connect (Tailscale's Go client compiled to WebAssembly, about 26 MB, imported only when someone signs in) to the TailscaleClient interface. Installs that package.

items.name: tailscale-controls
items.title: Tailscale controls
items.description: The Tailscale connection as controls, over useTailscale: a "Sign in with Tailscale" button that follows the connection (sign in, signing in and cancel, connected and sign out, error and retry), a status badge (inline, stacked or a pill) with the tailnet, the error and the sign-in link when a popup is blocked, and the parts of a connection panel: TailscaleSummary (tailnet and this device) and TailscaleExitNodes, a listbox of exit nodes like macOS's Wi-Fi menu, with an EmptyState when the tailnet offers none.

items.name: tailscale-fake
items.title: Fake Tailscale client
items.description: An in-memory TailscaleClient for tests, stories and demos: a sign-in that approves itself, auth keys, a node state map, and per-host request handlers. No network and no account.

items.name: tailscale-router
items.title: Tailscale request router
items.description: A service worker that intercepts the page's fetches, sends the ones its policy matches to a page connected to the tailnet over a MessagePort, and streams the answers back; everything else goes to the network untouched. Installs tailscale-sw.js into public/.

items.name: tailscale
items.title: Tailscale
items.description: Sign in to a tailnet from the browser: a controller (createTailscale) with a sign-in state machine (interactive login URL in a popup, or a pre-auth key from your server), a lazily created tailnet client behind a small structural interface, session persistence that can be encrypted in the passkey vault, a routing policy (*.ts.net, 100.64.0.0/10, your hosts and subnets), exit node helpers (pickExitNode) and React hooks (TailscaleProvider, useTailscale, useTailscaleStatus, useTailscaleFetch).

items.name: terminal-line
items.title: Terminal line discipline
items.description: Line editing, history, completion, Ctrl-C and a prompt, for a terminal with no PTY behind it: pure functions, and a shell that ties them to a command handler and outlives the component showing it.

items.name: terminal
items.title: Terminal
items.description: A real terminal emulator on wterm, themed from the library's tokens in light and dark. It fills its container and refits as that resizes. Connect it to a PTY with onData and write, or run whole lines with no PTY: prompt and onCommand add line editing, history, completion and Ctrl-C.

items.name: text-morph
items.title: TextMorph
items.description: A text label that morphs into the next one: shared letters slide to their new places, the rest blur out and in, and the box springs to the new width.

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: Multi-line sibling of Input on UI SDK's Textarea, with three minimum heights, the same focus, invalid and disabled states, auto resize and a submit shortcut.

items.name: theme
items.title: Theme
items.description: BLProvider, ThemeScope and the appearance context: pick light/dark, a tint and a theme scope for a subtree. BLProvider is also the layer host its popups stay inside (useLayerHost), and a size-class scope: it measures its own box and provides compact / medium / regular to everything inside, which presentation="auto" popups follow. Colors are shadcn variables (see the bl-theme item for the iOS palette).

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: Banners and HUDs on UI SDK's Toast: cards that pile up at an edge and spread on hover, the "Copied" pill that updates in place, with actions, promise toasts, swipe to dismiss, timers that pause on hover and focus, and announcements.

items.name: toggle
items.title: Toggle
items.description: UI SDK's Toggle, a button that stays pressed: tinted when on, in default, filled, outline and quiet (toolbar) variants with Button's sizes, with ToggleIcon and a controller; and ToggleGroup, toggles that share one value, single or multiple, one tab stop with arrow keys between them, as spaced toggles, a joined outline frame or Segmented's track (variant="segmented"), in a row or a column.

items.name: toolbar
items.title: Toolbar
items.description: A row of controls with one tab stop on UI SDK's Toolbar: plain, a floating card, or the iOS bottom bar of a list in edit mode.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: A small inverted label that names or describes a control on hover or keyboard focus, on UI SDK's Tooltip: a warm-up delay, an arrow toward the trigger, an optional shortcut hint; touch never opens it.

items.name: trace-timeline-model
items.title: Trace timeline model
items.description: The math and drawing behind TraceTimeline: linear and by-what-happened axes, stop selection and clustering, per-pixel pooling by binary search over sorted arrays, scrub speeds and re-anchoring, ruler ticks and time formatting, and one canvas drawing for both orientations.

items.name: trace-timeline
items.title: TraceTimeline
items.description: A long session on one clock, drawn on a canvas at most one thing per device pixel: a strip with a ruler, diamonds, density with marks over it, thread activity fetched for the view, requests and several lanes, or the same timeline as a rail for narrow windows with stops as dashes that swell around the pointer, a scrub that slows as you pull away, and pinch and wheel zoom. A slider on UI SDK (its value with change and commit details, its keys, and a bindDrag scrub that Escape puts back), with the keyboard that implies; the view, the focused lane and the selected thread and request are the primitive's state too, each reported with UI SDK change details.

items.name: tree
items.title: Tree
items.description: UI SDK's Tree with the kit's rows: compose it from parts, or hand it nested items and it draws them virtualized, with indent guides, file-type icons, search, Git status, rename in place, a context menu and a hover preview per row, and drag and drop; a custom row per node (renderRow), loading rows and an empty state. Fits any hierarchy, not only files.

items.name: trigger-palette
items.title: Trigger palette
items.description: Lets a popup take its colors from the element that opened it (palette="trigger"): copies the trigger's theme scope and light or dark surface onto the popup.

items.name: tui-preview
items.title: TuiPreview
items.description: An OpenTUI terminal program run on demand in a sandboxed, opaque-origin frame by OpenTUI's WebAssembly renderer: Run / Stop, a light or dark terminal that follows the page (`appearance`), keyboard input, visible start-up and render errors, and the same runtime Docstream uses for `tui` code fences.

items.name: use-copy
items.title: useCopy
items.description: Copy text to the clipboard with a short-lived "Copied" state per key and an announcement, for copy buttons in rows and toolbars.

items.name: use-file-upload
items.title: useFileUpload
items.description: The file-upload logic behind FileUpload: the fileUpload primitive (definePrimitive) with rows for UI SDK's FileInput (queued, uploading, done, failed, and rejected with the reason in words, duplicates included), a concurrency-limited upload queue with abort, retry and controlled mode, a controller and agent actions (remove, retry, clear, uploadAll), the useFileUpload hook, an XMLHttpRequest adapter that reports real progress, and helpers (describeRules, rejectionMessage; sizes through the kit's formatFileSize).

items.name: use-paced
items.title: usePaced
items.description: The latest value of something that changes faster than React can render (a playhead dragged through thousands of steps), taken at a pace it can keep up with: at once when things are quiet, the newest every so often while values keep coming.

items.name: utils
items.title: Utilities
items.description: BL UI's class-name helpers: cn (clsx + tailwind-merge that knows the token utilities) and cx (the same under a UI SDK part's className).

items.name: video-preview
items.title: VideoPreview
items.description: Plays a video timeline live, without rendering: the clips near the playhead as video, audio and image elements in their frames, with looks as CSS filters and fades as opacity and volume, following a shared playback clock (re-synced on drift, the next clip loaded ahead). With transport controls on the kit Toolbar and a timecode.

items.name: video-render
items.title: Video render
items.description: A timeline as one FFmpeg command: an input per clip, each picture fitted, looked, faded and laid over the background at its time, each sound retimed, levelled, faded, delayed and mixed, then MP4 (MPEG-4 + AAC), WebM (VP8 + Opus), GIF, MP3 or WAV. renderTimeline runs it with progress.

items.name: video-timeline-model
items.title: Video timeline model
items.description: The model behind VideoTimeline: tracks of clips (source in/out, speed, volume, fades, dissolves, picture-in-picture frames, colour looks), a magnetic main track whose edits ripple, and pure edits (split, trim, move, insert, remove, slice, snap) that return a new timeline, plus timecode and the looks as CSS and FFmpeg filters.

items.name: video-timeline
items.title: VideoTimeline
items.description: A video editor's timeline on UI SDK: clips are spans (createSpans) you drag along a track, among a magnetic track's clips (which make room) or to another track, with trim handles on both edges, frame-accurate edits snapping to edges and the playhead, keyboard moves and trims with one Tab stop for the clips and announcements; a ruler that is UI SDK's Slider for the playhead; lane headers (hide, mute, lock), which fold into a menu in a compact container; pinch or ⌘-wheel zoom and drops from a media library. value / onValueChange(value, details) once per gesture or key, so each edit is one undo step.

items.name: waveform
items.title: Waveform
items.description: Audio peaks drawn across a stretch of media time on a canvas, one bar per device pixel, mirrored or rising from the bottom, tinted by the text colour and scaled by a gain.

items.name: workspace
items.title: Workspace
items.description: Dockable tabs in resizable tabsets, from a layout you can save: UI SDK's Resizable for the splits and its Tabs for each tabset, with tabs that move along a strip, to another tabset or onto an edge to split it, by pointer or keyboard, and keep their state as they go.

items.name: apple-mail
items.title: Apple Mail clone
items.description: Apple Mail: Favorites, Smart Mailboxes and iCloud sections with rolling unread counts; a message list with unread dots, flags, attachments, previews and relative times; swipe actions (ListRow), edit mode, search and an unread filter; a message view with a quoted thread and reply, flag, move, archive and trash; and a compose sheet. One SplitView at every size: three tiled columns on desktop, an overlay sidebar on iPad, a stack with large titles and back buttons on iPhone. Composed from SplitView (sections, large titles), ListRow, Icon, SearchInput, Sheet, MarkdownEditor and DropdownMenu.

items.name: apple-music
items.title: Apple Music
items.description: Apple Music: Listen Now, Browse, Radio, Search and a Library (Recently Added, Artists, Albums, Songs, playlists) with generated album artwork, album, artist and playlist pages that tint from their artwork, and a mini player that springs open into the full Now Playing screen — scrubber, transport, volume, lyrics and up next — as one morphing element. Every song is a generated Strudel pattern (genre sets the band, the track seeds key, chords and melody) that really plays. A SplitView sidebar on desktop and tablet; the iOS tab bar with the mini player above it on phones; light and dark.

items.name: apple-notes
items.title: Apple Notes clone
items.description: Apple Notes for your Markdown files, with the Docstream rich editor. Add multiple folders under On My Mac; their handles are remembered across reloads. Each sidebar location is its own master list in a NavigationStack: folders push, file leaves open the note. The top-right control switches to the library's file Tree. Right-click any folder, note or location to rename, duplicate or delete it in place. The filter shows All Files or one type (Markdown, 3D models, images, JSON & YAML, spreadsheets, code & text); an STL model opens in a 3D viewer, an image in an image viewer, JSON or YAML in visual-json or as code (JSON edits save back to the file), a CSV or TSV in the library's GPU-sorted Spreadsheet, and source and text files in a code editor highlighted by gpu-lexer. Spreadsheet and code edits autosave (⌘S saves at once), and a file changed outside Notes reloads, or asks which copy to keep when you have edits. Embeds load from the note's folder, "Choose file…" picks any file in it, and dragging rows (or files from your computer) onto a note embeds them; drop computer files on a folder to copy them in, or drag files onto another location to move or copy them. Includes OPFS personal notes, autosave, native document properties, task state icons and menus, folder-backed live examples, unseen external-edit blue dots and conflict recovery. Starts with no sample content. Responsive SplitView on desktop, tablet and phone.

items.name: apple-passwords
items.title: Apple Passwords
items.description: Apple's Passwords app: category tiles with counts (All, Passkeys, Codes, Wi-Fi, Security, Deleted) and shared groups, a searchable item list, and a detail with copy buttons, a password that morphs into view, verification codes with a countdown ring, a “Copied” HUD, edit mode, security recommendations by severity, Wi-Fi networks with a QR code, and Developer Sign-In buttons (GitHub, Fly.io, Netlify, Replay) that run the real device-code logins, going through the tailnet when this tab is signed in to Tailscale with an exit node (the Safari block's node) and BL's CORS proxy (a Cloudflare Worker) otherwise, keep the tokens encrypted with a passkey, and check each token against its service; other blocks reuse that keychain through PasswordsKeychain and useKeychainSignIn (the GitHub clone reads its GitHub token there). Three columns on desktop, two on tablet, a pushed stack on phones; light and dark.

items.name: apple-reminders
items.title: Apple Reminders
items.description: Apple Reminders: smart-list tiles (Today, Scheduled, All, Flagged, Completed) with live counts, colored lists with sections, circular checkboxes that spring filled, inline add, a details sheet (notes, date and time, flag, priority, subtasks), show/clear completed, search, and a small burst when a list is cleared. Right-click any checkbox for every docstream task state (in progress, implemented, blocked, parked, refuted, verified, cancelled); the details sheet has the same Status menu. Markdown task lists become lists too: files in this browser's private store (OPFS) and in folders you add from your computer — both shared with the Apple Notes block — are scanned for `- [ ]` items, headings become sections, nested tasks subtasks, and every change is written back to that line of the file. Sidebar and list side by side on wide screens; the lists screen pushes the list on phones. Large list titles fold into the bar as you scroll; tints with each list's color, light and dark.

items.name: apple-settings
items.title: Apple Settings
items.description: iOS, iPadOS and macOS Settings in one block: search, an Apple Account header, inset groups with colored icon tiles, and drill-down panes with switches, sliders, pickers and segmented controls. One SplitView: macOS System Settings at desktop, an iPad split on tablets, and on phones the large-title list with panes pushing over it. Display & Brightness switches light and dark live.

items.name: cloudflare-studio
items.title: Cloudflare Studio
items.description: A system of Cloudflare's services as an app: search the catalog to add a service, drag from a Worker's env to what it binds, choose the operations it uses, and give anything that runs code an XState machine, edited in a StateDiagram, with what crosses each connection checked against what the machine receives. Export gives the system's JSON, a wrangler.jsonc for each Worker with what it still needs listed, and a module for each machine, as files: nothing's deployed and there's no account. It's kept in the browser as it changes, and works down to a phone's width, where the inspector is a page pushed over the board and Export is a sheet.

items.name: codex-clone
items.title: Codex clone
items.description: A chat-and-documents workspace in the style of Codex: an icon rail and chat list (New chat, Priority for chats with replies waiting), a chat with dot — link chips and cover cards for the documents it writes, streaming replies, a composer — and a document pane with an editable Markdown page, a checklist you can tick and a section outline in its margin (ticks that open a card of headings on hover). Every chat has its own workspace: picking another switches the document pane to that chat's documents, back on the section you left, and links between documents open in place. The sidebar has two forms — with the inbox (Priority, then chats), or without it (Projects as folders of threads, then Recents) — and a project thread fills the chat and document columns with a wide transcript, a turn rail whose dashes open a card with the message and its reply, and the thread's panel (Changes, Sources). Three tiled columns on desktop; chats → chat → document as a stack on a phone. Composed from SplitView, MarkdownEditor, DropdownMenu and the Workbench icon buttons.

items.name: delivery-tracking
items.title: Delivery tracking
items.description: An order card resting over a live map: a ProgressStepper walks through the delivery stages while the chat below answers questions about the order. Composed from ArtifactChatContainer, FloatingSheet and ProgressStepper.

items.name: discord-clone
items.title: Discord clone
items.description: A team chat in Discord's shape: server rail, channel sidebar with threads, a transcript with reactions and thread previews, a member list, and a thread panel that docks on wide screens and slides over on narrow ones. Composed from ChatShell, Tabs, Avatar and the Composer, with its own channel, message and member parts; messages are rendered by Docstream.

items.name: freeform
items.title: Freeform
items.description: An infinite whiteboard after Apple's Freeform: a gallery of boards, and a pannable, zoomable canvas of sticky notes, shapes, text, photos, links, connectors that follow what they're glued to, and freehand drawing on PencilKit. Select, move, resize, rotate, group, lock, align and arrange; alignment guides while you drag; Format panel for fills, borders, text, connectors and the board's background; undo and redo per board; scroll to pan, pinch or ⌘-scroll to zoom. Built on the PencilKit core (strokes, inks, tool palette).

items.name: github-clone
items.title: GitHub clone
items.description: A GitHub repository page over GitHub's real data: signed in with GitHub in the Passwords keychain (the same passkey-encrypted device sign-in the Passwords block and the docs use, so no second sign-in), it reads any repository you pick — owner/name, a github.com URL, or your recently pushed ones — straight from the GitHub REST API: README and file browser with a code viewer per branch, issue and pull request lists with labels and counts, an issue or pull request conversation (comments, commits, labels, review requests, reviews, merges) whose comment composer posts real comments, reviewers, checks and a merge box, a unified diff for Files changed, and Actions runs. Loading, rate-limit, not-found and signed-out states; responses cached for the session. Without a sign-in it shows an invented sample repository, offline, with a Sign in with GitHub button. Primer colors in light and dark; collapses to a phone layout with pushed screens.

items.name: interface-builder
items.title: Interface Builder
items.description: Xcode's storyboard for React apps made of BL UI: scenes on a canvas composed from the kit's own components and containers (NavigationStack, Tabs, SplitView, lists), edited in place; segues, delegates, outlets, the first responder and context in React's terms; Framer-style motion with spring and easing editors and a timeline; Google Fonts typography with live preview; a live preview, and the app as code.

items.name: loop-qa
items.title: Loop QA
items.description: An agentic QA workspace after Loop QA / Replay QA. Projects (a URL under test) with drawn site thumbnails, bug trends and live-run state; per project an Overview (tiles, the live run, an exploration replay carousel, latest findings), a filterable Bugs table (severity, status, kind, environment; copy, download and connect an issue tracker), a Site map tree with coverage, Test runs and generated Playwright tests with highlighted source. A bug opens to its session replay (ReplayPreview: scrubber markers for the failed request and the error, a drawn cursor with click ripples), network and console logs that seek the replay, expected vs actual, a chronology whose evidence frames are the replay frozen at each step, and the root cause; a run to its findings, coverage, exploration and journeys. The Ask QA agent is an ArtifactChatContainer around the app (the page is the artifact): a trailing column on a desktop, a floating composer over the page on a tablet or phone with the transcript on its draggable bump (the newest reply peeking on a tablet), folded into a FAB when hidden; tool calls in a work log, streamed Markdown answers, and runs that report live in a card. ⌘K jumps to any project, bug or run and runs commands (start a run, copy reports, change a bug's status or severity, connect a tracker, switch the theme) across nested pages with a bug preview pane. One SplitView at every size — tiled on a desktop, a floating sidebar on a tablet, a stack on a phone; light and dark.

items.name: macos
items.title: macOS
items.description: A macOS desktop whose apps are the other examples — Reminders, Mail, Safari, Notes, Music, Passwords, System Settings, Time Machine, Maps, Delivery, Freeform, GitHub, Discord, Codex, VS Code, OpenCode, T3 Code and Loop QA. Open one from the Dock or from Alfred and it appears in a window you can drag, resize, zoom, minimize and stack (right-click the Dock to turn magnification off or hiding on — a hidden Dock slides up from the bottom edge and windows take its room); the menu bar follows the frontmost app, and its Tailscale and Wi-Fi items are working menus. The desktop owns one Tailscale controller (the real Tailscale by default; its WebAssembly client loads only when someone signs in) that Safari, VS Code and the menu bar share, so signing in or choosing an exit node in either shows in both: the Tailscale menu is the core TailscaleExitNodes, with exit nodes drawn like Wi-Fi networks (a check for the one in use, the name, a signal glyph, Connecting…), and the Wi-Fi menu is invented sample data in the same row style — a switch, the network you are on, nearby ones with locks and signal bars, and Network Settings…. Alfred is the launcher on top, built on the CommandMenu primitive: type an app's name and press Enter, or use its pages — a calculator with live results and history (type math at the root and the answer shows inline), clipboard history with a preview pane, pinning (⌘P) and delete (⌘⌫), an emoji grid you move through with the arrow keys, snippets that expand from ;keywords, file search with folders you open with → and reveal with ⌘↵, system commands (lock screen, sleep, empty Trash with a confirmation, dark mode, restart), web searches, and multi-step workflows (create a GitHub issue, start a timer). ⌥Space hides and shows the bar, and a HUD confirms each copy. Every session is recorded with rrweb into append-only localStorage streams, and Time Machine plays them back; apps load on first launch. Below 640px wide the desktop turns into an iPhone — a status bar with the Dynamic Island, a springboard of the same apps (paged when they don't fit, with a dock and a Search pill that opens Alfred), full-screen apps that zoom out of their icons, and a home bar that sends one back while it keeps running. Light and dark.

items.name: map-chat
items.title: Map chat
items.description: An always-floating chat over a slippy map: the guide answers with tool calls that pan, zoom, pin and route the map (walking times, distances, saved trips). Composed from ArtifactChatContainer and a small tile-map renderer with its own geo maths, places and tool-planning agent; the map navigates on UI SDK's viewport (drag, pinch, scroll and Ctrl/⌘-scroll or pinch to zoom, and on the focused map the arrow keys pan, + and − zoom and 0 returns to the view). Needs network for the map tiles.

items.name: pencilkit-sketch
items.title: PencilKit sketch pad
items.description: A freehand sketch pad: dotted paper, a PencilCanvas and the floating PencilToolbar (tools, inks, widths, undo and redo). Composed from PencilCanvas, PencilToolbar and usePencilHistory.

items.name: replay-canvas
items.title: Replay Canvas
items.description: An app taken apart from its rrweb recordings, on a Figma-style canvas. Every recording is read for the pages it visits, the layers that open over them (dialogs, menus, sheets, popovers, toasts, found by being added at the top of the body or revealed by a class or attribute) and the states they go through; each frame is the recording itself (ReplayStage) paused at that moment, a layer cropped to just its panel and laid out beside the page it opened over. Segues run from where the click landed to what it opened, labelled with what was clicked: navigate, present, update and dismiss. Recordings fold into one map — pages by route pattern (/projects/:id), title or skeleton, layers by kind, structure and buttons, states by the control that led to them — so every recording added confirms what's there (counted) and fills in what isn't. Select a frame or segue to see the moments it was seen at and play the recording from there in ReplayPreview; drop more rrweb .json files anywhere to add them. Signed in to Replay, it lists your Replay QA projects and their test runs; pick a test run to load the recording of every journey in it. Hide the arrows to see only the dots where clicks landed; select a dot to draw its arrow. Rest the pointer on a frame, a segue, a recording or a test run for a hover card about it; a minimap in the corner shows the whole map and moves the view. An update that changes one part of a page (a switch, a row) is a frame of just that part, and chrome every page shares (a header, a sidebar, by landmark or by layout) is drawn once, with what's clicked in it leading to the pages. Segues are colored by journey (recording): where journeys share one they run side by side, and pressing a journey's dot follows it, its steps numbered and the rest faded. Sample: four sessions of a mock project tracker.

items.name: replay-debugger
items.title: Replay Debugger
items.description: A time-travel debugger with forward and reverse stepping, source navigation, breakpoints, logpoints, call stacks, scopes and expression evaluation. A plain DebuggerHost interface supplies data and callbacks; the included demo answers from an in-memory table.

items.name: saas-checkout
items.title: SaaS checkout
items.description: A Stripe-style upgrade flow: plans billed monthly or yearly at a per-seat price with a seat stepper, an account step, then card payment — the number groups itself and shows its brand, with expiry, security code, country and postal code. The order summary follows along live (promotion codes, tax from the billing address, the total); a mock processor takes the payment, its test cards decline in different ways, and the flow ends on a receipt. A sticky summary beside the form on wide hosts; one column with the summary folded into a bar on narrow ones. Nothing leaves the browser.

items.name: safari
items.title: Safari clone
items.description: A browser that only browses through your tailnet. Opening it shows a gate: nothing works until Tailscale is connected (a saved session is restored without a prompt; signing out brings the gate back), and behind it the browser is inert. Then a tabbed Safari: back and forward with per-tab history, an address field with suggestions from your tailnet's devices and your history, reload and stop, a tab strip and a tab overview, a start page of your devices with a Tailscale report, and a popover (TailscaleSummary, TailscaleExitNodes and TailscaleLoginButton) to see or end the connection and choose the exit node. Pages run: Safari mounts the Tailscale request router with a proxyPath and opens each page in a frame at <your site>/__tailnet/<scheme>/<host>/<path>, where its service worker serves the document and routes every request the page makes (scripts, fetches, relative URLs, styles, images) through the tailnet; a script it injects keeps links and forms in the proxy and reports the address and title back, so history follows the page. The page runs on your origin (it can read your storage); cookies are not kept and WebSockets are not routed. Where no service worker can run, pages fall back to sealed documents (scripts removed, assets inlined). It uses the real Tailscale by default: Tailscale's own client as WebAssembly and its real sign-in page. A tailnet alone reaches your devices; for the public internet an exit node carries the traffic and the DNS lookups, and Safari picks one for you: opening a public address with none set selects the best online exit node (the one used last, else the first by name) and loads the page. The shield menu (TailscaleExitNodes) changes or clears it; choosing None is remembered, so a public address then explains why it fails, and Try Again turns an exit node back on (it also swaps an offline or failing exit node for another online one). With no online exit node it fails with an explanation. A simulated tailnet (data.ts) is there for stories and tests, never the default. The address field is UI SDK’s Combobox. The gate is a modal Dialog contained in Safari's BLProvider (a layer host), and ⌘L, ⌘R, ⌘[ and ⌘] are shortcuts scoped to the focused browser. Composed from TailscaleProvider, the Tailscale request router, TailscaleSummary, TailscaleExitNodes, TailscaleLoginButton, Button, Combobox, Dialog, Popover, Spinner, Icon and BLProvider.

items.name: split-view-demos
items.title: SplitView compositions
items.description: Six compositions of SplitView in one switcher: Mail (three columns), Notes (two columns), Settings (sidebar and detail), Reminders (tinted rows, large titles), Music library (a push/pop stack inside the detail) and a Notes gallery whose list steps aside. Each is a plain composition of the public SplitView parts.

items.name: strudel-studio
items.title: Strudel Studio
items.description: A live-coding music studio: write Strudel and play it on skeuomorphic hardware generated from the code's syntax tree — a rack of modules with LED-ring knobs, channel faders, backlit mute/solo pads and TR-style step keys on a masonry grid you drag and resize. Every control rewrites the code while it plays; a syntax-tree tab shows the parsed song. Four starter songs.

items.name: t3-clone
items.title: T3 Code clone
items.description: An IDE-style agent workspace in the style of T3 Code: thread sidebar, streaming conversation with a composer that flies from centre to dock, resizable terminal dock with tabs, a surface panel (browser, terminal, files, diff, agents) — every thread keeps its own terminals and panel surface, so picking another thread switches them too — and a ⌘K command palette with nested pages (new thread in a project, link pull requests, go to file, search contents, add a project from a local folder, Git URL or GitHub) plus a live theme editor. Docks everything on desktop, slides the panel in as a drawer on tablets, and moves to a hamburger sidebar, bottom tab bar and dismissible-sheet terminal on phones. Composed from the WorkbenchShell, conversation, terminal and surface primitives, with its own thread sidebar parts.

items.name: timemachine
items.title: Time Machine
items.description: Every session of the macOS desktop, recorded and kept to watch again. Each page load is recorded with rrweb as an append-only stream in localStorage — private to the browser by default — and this app lists the sessions by day and plays any one in a ReplayPreview. Turn on Cloud sync to mirror the streams live to a Durable Streams server (Rivet) so another device can watch too. The app is marked rr-block and rr-ignore, so the recorder never records itself replaying.

items.name: vibecoder
items.title: Vibecoder
items.description: OpenCode v2.2.4 and a live app in one browser workspace. Provider sign-ins, the Tailscale device and exit node restore from the shared encrypted Passwords keychain after unlocking. The terminal and starter HTTP server start on mount. Edit the same AlmostNode files from OpenCode and preview the running app through AlmostNode's service worker. Configurable AlmostNode or agent-wasm host bridge, port switching, reload and terminal lifecycle controls.

items.name: video-editor
items.title: Video Editor
items.description: A video editor in the browser, after iMovie and Final Cut: a media library (drop or browse for video, audio and images), a viewer that plays the edit live, an inspector (volume, speed, fades, dissolves, colour looks, fill or fit, picture in picture, titles) and a timeline with a magnetic main track, titles over it and music under it: drag to move, trim the edges, split, snap, zoom, undo. FFmpeg in WebAssembly (openclaw/ffmpeg-wasm, built by tools/ffmpeg-wasm) runs in workers on the device to probe files, draw filmstrips and waveforms, and export the timeline to MP4, WebM, GIF, MP3 or WAV with live progress. Its threads need a cross-origin isolated page; without one the browser plays what it can and export is off.

items.name: vscode
items.title: VS Code
items.description: A VS Code window that really runs: an activity rail with Explorer, Search and Run, editors in a Workspace you can split, and wterm terminals where opencode opens the real OpenCode TUI on the same files. A Tailscale status-bar menu connects terminal fetches to your tailnet and shares the desktop connection inside macOS. It runs on one in-browser Node runtime (agent-wasm, the fork of almostnode). Everything it needs goes through one interface, so a real folder and real shells can replace the runtime. Packages you install run in a Worker. Where the host serves it with CORS, as GitHub Pages does, that Worker has an opaque origin and no access to the site's storage; elsewhere it's an ordinary Worker of the site that can read and change the site's IndexedDB and caches, and the status bar says which. They can use the network either way, as far as CORS allows.

items.name: worktree-atlas
items.title: Worktree Atlas
items.description: Every Git worktree under the folders you open, grouped by repository, running entirely in the browser: open folders with the File System Access API (remembered across visits) and Git is read in the page by isomorphic-git, no server or desktop app. The sidebar folds each project open to its worktrees (five at first, Show more for twenty, then twenty more at a time), with a rail that switches between Files and Changes. Right-click a worktree to delete it; every delete goes through a confirmation dialog that checks for uncommitted changes first and, like git worktree remove, keeps dirty ones unless you choose otherwise, keeps locked ones, and only prunes missing ones. The master column is the open worktree's file Tree: every file in the checkout (Files, with search and uncommitted changes marked) or what it changes against main since it branched (Changes, with a summary of ahead/behind and line counts). The detail shows the picked file, highlighted, or every change in a virtualized @pierre/diffs CodeView, unified or split. Pluggable WorktreeSource (sample data included) so a desktop app can supply Git CLI results instead. Responsive SplitView on desktop, tablet and phone.
